label: Betrayal
framing: Betrayal is a wound the betrayer chose to give you, and Scripture does not rush past it. It records the friend who turned, the kiss that handed Jesus over, the psalmist undone not by an enemy but by a companion he once walked with to the house of God.
cultural: In the ancient world a shared meal and a covenant of friendship were nearly sacred bonds, so to betray someone you had eaten with was among the deepest of treacheries. That is why the Psalms cry out so bitterly against the close friend who lifted his heel, and why the Gospels mark that it was at the table, after the bread, that Judas went out into the night.
historical: The church has never told the betrayed to pretend they were not betrayed. The Psalms of betrayal have been prayed in worship for three thousand years, the desert fathers warned how betrayal can curdle into a bitterness that consumes the wounded one, and pastors across the centuries have held two things at once, that the wrong was real and that the wounded heart must not be left forever in the betrayer's grip.
application: Do not minimize what was done to you, and do not let anyone hurry you to a forgiveness you have not yet reached. Take the wound to God in the raw language of the Psalms, which give you permission to say it all. Forgiveness, when it comes, is releasing the debt to the just Judge, not declaring the wound small, and it is not the same as rebuilt trust, which is earned slowly and sometimes never. You can release the debt and still set a wise boundary.

verses.text: For it is not an enemy who insults me; that I could endure. It is not a foe who rises against me; from him I could hide. But it is you, a man like myself, my companion and close friend. We shared sweet fellowship together; we walked with the crowd into the house of God.
verses.where: The psalmist says he could have endured an insult from an enemy, or hidden from a foe; but it was his companion and close friend, with whom he once walked into the house of God. The site's note says his deepest wound is that the attack comes not from an enemy but from a friend. Scripture names the particular cruelty of betrayal: it comes from inside the circle of trust.

verses.text: Even my close friend whom I trusted, the one who shared my bread, has lifted up his heel against me.
verses.where: A sick man says that even his close friend, the one who shared his bread, has lifted his heel against him. The site's plain note admits that his next words may be a raw wish to repay, and adds that Jesus, betrayed by a friend at table, still washed that friend's feet (John 13:5). The Bible records how betrayal feels without pretending the feeling is the last word.

verses.text: Now someone told David: “Ahithophel is among the conspirators with Absalom.” So David pleaded, “O LORD, please turn the counsel of Ahithophel into foolishness!”
verses.where: Driven from Jerusalem by his own son's conspiracy, David climbs the Mount of Olives weeping, barefoot and with his head covered, and then learns that his trusted counselor Ahithophel has joined the conspirators. His answer is a prayer that God would turn that counsel into foolishness. The site's note says that on the same road he sends his friend Hushai back into the city to work against that counsel: he weeps, he prays, and he acts.

verses.text: But Jesus asked him, “Judas, are you betraying the Son of Man with a kiss?”
verses.where: Judas comes at the head of a crowd and draws near to kiss Jesus, and Jesus asks whether he is betraying the Son of Man with a kiss. The site's note says Luke does not narrate the kiss itself, and that Jesus names the act for what it is. The sign of friendship became the means of betrayal, and Jesus does not pretend otherwise.

verses.text: But as for me, I will look to the LORD; I will wait for the God of my salvation. My God will hear me.
verses.where: The prophet laments a land where friends cannot be trusted, where a man's enemies are the members of his own household. The site's note says that in the middle of that he resolves to wait for the God of his salvation. When every human trust seems to fail, Micah does not stop trusting; he moves his trust to the one who will hear him.

verses.text: Like a broken tooth or a foot out of joint is confidence in a faithless man in time of trouble.
verses.where: A proverb from the collection copied by King Hezekiah's scribes compares confidence in a faithless person in time of trouble to a broken tooth or a foot out of joint. You lean on it at the moment you need it, and it gives way and hurts. Wisdom here is not cynicism but care about where you put your weight.

verses.text: At my first defense, no one stood with me, but everyone deserted me. May it not be charged against them. But the Lord stood by me and strengthened me, so that through me the message would be fully proclaimed, and all the Gentiles would hear it. So I was delivered from the mouth of the lion.
verses.where: Facing death, Paul writes that at his first defense everyone deserted him, and prays that it not be charged against them; but the Lord stood by him. The site's plain note says he forgave those who failed out of fear, left Alexander, who did him great harm, to God's justice, and warned Timothy to protect himself. It adds that these verses never ask anyone to stay near someone who has done them great harm or to keep silent.

verses.text: Then Peter remembered the word that Jesus had spoken: “Before the rooster crows, you will deny Me three times.” And he went outside and wept bitterly.
verses.where: Peter, who had sworn he would never deny Jesus, denies him three times before the rooster crows, then remembers and goes out and weeps bitterly. The site's plain note asks whether his failure was the end of him, and answers that it was not: after the resurrection Jesus sent word to his brothers, and Peter was among them. Some who read this page are the ones who betrayed, and Scripture does not leave them out.

verses.text: Jesus asked a third time, “Simon son of John, do you love Me?” Peter was deeply hurt that Jesus had asked him a third time, “Do you love Me?” “Lord, You know all things,” he replied. “You know I love You.” Jesus said to him, “Feed My sheep.
verses.where: Beside a charcoal fire, as the denials were, the risen Jesus asks Peter three times whether he loves him, and three times gives him back his work. The site's note says the three denials are answered by three confessions. All the churches agree, the plain note says, that Peter failed and Jesus restored him: restoration came through truth, grief and a renewed calling, not by pretending nothing had happened.

verses.text: Cast your burden upon the LORD and He will sustain you; He will never let the righteous be shaken.
verses.where: The same psalm that names the betraying friend ends by urging the reader to cast his burden on the LORD, who will sustain him. The site's note says the psalmist hands the matter to God and does not take revenge himself. The wound is not denied; it is carried to someone strong enough to carry it.

misread.taken: Jesus' command to forgive seven times in a day is used to tell someone who keeps being betrayed or hurt that they must forgive again, trust again, and go back, as often as the other person says sorry.
misread.says: The site's plain note says forgiveness has been misused in exactly this way, and that this is not what the passage asks. Jesus first says to rebuke the one who sins: forgiveness names the wrong and then refuses to hold it over the other person. It lets go of revenge, but it is not the same as trusting someone again, and it does not mean a crime should go unreported. The note adds that a person who says I repent again and again for the same harm, and keeps doing it, has not turned at all, and that words alone do not make it safe to stay.
misread.text: Even if he sins against you seven times in a day, and seven times returns to say, ‘I repent,’ you must forgive him.”

whole: If the person who betrayed you is also harming you, threatening you or controlling you, your safety comes first: tell someone you trust and get help, and the Find Help page on this site lists places to turn. Where a crime has been done, it is right to report it. Betrayal comes in many shapes: a spouse's affair, a friend who told your secret, a business partner who took what was yours, a pastor who used your trust, a parent who sided with the one who hurt you. It is a particular wound because it comes from inside the circle of trust. It rewrites the past, so that old memories have to be checked for what was really happening. It makes a person doubt their own judgment, and sometimes it makes them afraid to trust anyone at all.

Scripture does not rush past betrayal. It records the companion of Psalm 55, the friend who shared bread and lifted his heel, Ahithophel joining Absalom's conspiracy, and Judas coming with a kiss. Behind the betrayals it shows are the ordinary engines of sin: envy, greed, fear, ambition, desire indulged until it outweighs a promise. It also shows betrayal from the other side. Peter swore he would never deny Jesus, and denied him three times before morning. Most of us have broken a confidence or a promise somewhere, and remembering that does not make what was done to us small. It keeps us from imagining that betrayal is something only other people do.

So the Bible's wisdom is to name the wrong truthfully, grieve it honestly, and refuse both revenge and pretense. Jesus named Judas's act for what it was; the psalmist poured out his betrayal to God and handed the matter over rather than taking revenge. Forgiveness, when it comes, lets go of the debt, but it is not the same as trust, and trust is rebuilt, if at all, only by trustworthiness shown over time; Proverbs warns that leaning on a faithless person is like leaning on a broken tooth. You may need distance, and you may need to protect others from the one who betrayed you. Take care where you put your weight now, without deciding that no one can be trusted. And if you are the one who betrayed, Peter's road is open to you: the whole truth, bitter tears, and the slow work of showing that your love is real.

The hope Scripture gives is that Jesus himself knows this wound from the inside. He was betrayed by a friend at table and deserted by the rest, and he went on to the cross for the very people who failed him. When everyone deserted Paul, the Lord stood by him. And the risen Christ met Peter beside a charcoal fire and gave him back his calling. That does not mean every betrayal will be mended in this life. It means that God is faithful when people are not, that he will judge rightly what was done to you, and that the one who was betrayed is never left alone.
deep.sit: Where have you put your weight since this happened, and what would it look like to trust God with the wrong without either taking revenge or pretending it did not happen?

prayer.lead: The prayer of the man betrayed by his companion, calling to God morning, noon and night. Pray it when the betrayal will not leave your mind.
prayer.text: But I call to God, and the LORD saves me. Morning, noon, and night, I cry out in distress, and He hears my voice. He redeems my soul in peace from the battle waged against me, even though many oppose me.

careLines.text: A person can forgive and still stay safe, still tell the truth, and still ask for justice.
Words alone do not make it safe to stay.
Where a crime has been done, it is right to report it to the authorities.
The Find Help page on this site lists places to turn.
